# Antigravity Kit - Architecture

> Multi-AI base kit. `.agent/` is the single source of truth; every other AI sees it through symlinks.

<!-- kit-counts:start -->
**130 agents** · **210 skills** · **111 workflows** · **34 scripts inside skills** (generated by `.agent/scripts/sync_entrypoints.py --write-docs`)
<!-- kit-counts:end -->

## The three building blocks

| Block | What it is | Where it lives | Who triggers it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Skill** | Knowledge/procedure the AI loads when the task matches its `description` (can ship `scripts/`, `references/`) | `.agent/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | The AI, automatically |
| **Agent** | A specialist *role* (persona + tools + preloaded skills). Needs `name` (= filename) and `description` | `.agent/agents/<name>.md` | The AI delegates, or you mention `@name` |
| **Workflow** | A saved procedure you run by typing `/name` (a "slash command"). Needs `description` | `.agent/workflows/<name>.md` | You, manually (`disable-model-invocation: true`) |

Rule of thumb: *who does it* = agent; *how to do it* = skill; *a button I press* = workflow.

## Multi-AI exposure

Each AI reads a different folder. Never copy; symlink (script does it):

| AI | Rules | Skills | Agents | Workflows / commands |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google Antigravity | `.agent/rules/GEMINI.md` | `.agent/skills/` | `.agent/agents/` | `.agent/workflows/` |
| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | `.claude/skills/` | `.claude/agents/` | `.claude/commands/` |
| Cursor | `.cursorrules` | reads `.claude/skills/` | reads `.claude/agents/` | `.cursor/commands/` |
| Codex / OpenCode / others | `AGENTS.md` | - | - | - |

Rule files (`CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.agent/rules/*`) must stay identical: `sync_rules.py`.

## Scripts

- **Inside skills** (`.agent/skills/<skill>/scripts/`): everything that belongs to one domain (security_scan, lint_runner, ux_audit, seo_checker, ...). The skill that owns the topic owns the script.
- **`.agent/scripts/`**: only cross-cutting orchestrators:
  - `checklist.py` / `verify_all.py` - run the skill scripts in priority order
  - `sync_rules.py` - rule-file parity
  - `sync_entrypoints.py` - symlinks + validation (`--check`, `--write-docs`)
  - `projects_audit.py`, `session_manager.py`, `auto_preview.py`

## Keeping it consistent

After adding, renaming or removing a skill, agent or workflow:

```bash
python .agent/scripts/sync_entrypoints.py --write-docs   # symlinks + validation + counts
python .agent/scripts/sync_rules.py                      # only if a rule file changed
```

`sync_entrypoints.py --check` validates frontmatter, `skills:` references in agents and script paths used by `checklist.py`; it exits 1 on any error (usable as a pre-commit/CI step).

## Other folders

- `.agent/plans/` - execution loops, handoffs, audits (see CLAUDE.md "Plans & Audits Convention")
- `.agent/workflows/_arquivo/` - retired workflows, not exposed to any AI
- `projetos/` - one sheet per project that uses this kit; `projetos/prompts/` are the prompts that sync projects with the kit
